title: Add intake telemetry sparsifier and release prioritizer
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Introduces telemetry sparsifier and cohort prioritizer to reduce changelog noise and surface high-impact variant changes. Includes CLI hook for release assembler and rollout safety checks.
description:
Motivation: onboarding churn and high-cardinality telemetry made autogenerated changelogs noisy. Teams spend time triaging small profile deltas that don't affect customers. This PR adds a telemetry sparsifier and a cohort-aware release prioritizer that (1) reduces telemetry volume for onboarding signals, (2) scores variant deltas by customer impact and statistical significance, and (3) produces prioritized changelog fragments for the release assembler.

Summary of changes (single string): Implemented a lightweight 'sparsifier' daemon that ingests intake telemetry and emits sampled, TTL-bound summaries; added a cohort-calibrator that maps variant keys -> affinity cohorts using usage-weighted clustering; introduced a priority scorer that combines delta magnitude, cohort exposure, and drift persistence to rank release note candidates; provided a CLI hook (bin/registry-release-prioritize) to emit prioritized changelog fragments consumed by the release assembler; added unit and integration tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc and migration notes (docs/onboard/sparsifier-design.md)
- [x] Telemetry ingestion + sparsifier service (pkg/telemetry/sparsifier.go)
- [x] Cohort calibrator + mapper (pkg/registry/cohort_calibrator.go)
- [x] Prioritizer + CLI hook (cmd/release-prioritizer/main.go)
- [x] Release assembler integration test (integration/release_prioritizer_test.go)
- [x] Add feature flag and rollout plan for one-week canary

Design notes: The sparsifier applies adaptive reservoir sampling keyed by (model_alias, variant_stamp, customer_id_hash) with a configurable signal-to-noise threshold. Samples carry a small fingerprint (sha1) and a short histogram (latency quantiles) rather than full traces, and are TTL'd after 7 days by default. The cohort calibrator uses an L2-normalized usage vector across endpoints to cluster variants into 8 cohorts; cohort size and cluster count are runtime-configurable. The prioritizer computes a score = w1*delta_score + w2*cohort_exposure + w3*persistence_score where weights default to {0.5,0.35,0.15} and are exposed in the console. A minimum significance filter avoids surfacing small statistical fluctuations.

Example prioritized fragment (what the CLI emits): 
{ "model": "open-analog-1.2", "variant": "quant-int8-a", "score": 0.87, "reason": "increased latency for cohort-B (10% exposure)" }

Operational concerns and rollout: the sparsifier runs behind a feature flag (registry.sparsifier.enabled) and is namespace-isolated. Default sampling is conservative (0.1%) for new models; we will run a 7-day canary on non-prod datacenters and monitor the release-assembler mismatch metric and "changelog-noise" alert. We added a safety fallback: if the prioritizer's top-n score is below threshold, the release assembler will fall back to the previous delta-based behavior.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover sampling edge cases and cohort mapping; an integration test exercises the CLI -> assembler handoff with synthetic telemetry. Performance: local bench shows sparsifier adds ~1ms p95 to intake path when running as sidecar; CPU/alloc profiles included in PR artifacts.

Related work and follow-ups: follow-up will add per-customer exposure quotas, an optional human-in-the-loop review UI in Console, and a telemetry export for auditors.
